_comment: SSOT for DISPATCHABLE models on every transport, host included (the `anthropic` transport was added 2026-09-04; before that this file was external-only): per-transport role resolution, prices, limits, authorization gates, and model IDENTITY -- one row per model version (label, family, version, lifecycle, display order, cost rank), and `aliasHistory` for which id each alias served when. Policy prose home: .claude/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md section 5. Registry `roles` owns each row's tier claims; the ladder in `.claude/reference/model_ladder_evidence.md` owns tier definitions, model judgment and effort; this file owns per-transport resolution. A bare alias names the CURRENT version of its family on every route; a superseded version keeps its row under a versioned alias (opus5, sol56, luna56). A version move is therefore an edit here: a new row that takes its family's roles and effort (effort.measuredVersion names the predecessor), an alias remap and an aliasHistory boundary. The ladder's family row needs no edit until a cell or an owner ruling shows the new version differs. `prior` is an intake input (frontier|mid|small), never a measurement: rows without an owner statement take their tier. Owner capability claims use effort.evidence owner with effort.evidenceRef holding an ISO date and quoted owner words or a transcript/decision-ledger citation. The optional row field `probation` is a hand edit by the owner, or by an agent carrying the owner's quoted instruction, never an agent's own judgment. `probation` [{tier, text, evidenceRef}] marks a row on probation for a tier (definition: .claude/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md section 5); read it with model_registry.py review-state. Validate with: python3 .claude/tools/model_registry.py --check

modelAttestation._comment: A proxied child CANNOT report which model served it. Claude Code's system prompt asserts a Claude identity, so the arm parrots it; worse, a run with CCP_CODEX_MODEL forcing gpt-5.6-luna reported `modelUsage: [gpt-5.4-mini]` — the child's own pin, not the served model. Any void-check reading modelUsage mislabels the arm. The proxy's own capture is the only valid attestation.

serverSidePins._comment: Model and effort are forced at the PROXY, not via the child's --model, so a role-name pin cannot silently redirect an arm: this transport's alias surface accepts `opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`/`fable` and full `claude-*` ids as aliases onto GPT models, inverting DeepSeek's behavior of hard-erroring on them. opencode._limitsSource: models.dev, the OpenCode team's own catalog (first-party metadata, not a benchmark) - written by the retired Zen-direct refresh; this transport is unavailable and no tool refreshes it. Recorded once here because ONE catalog sourced every row on this transport.
opencode._comment: OpenCode Zen FREE tier (https://opencode.ai/zen) — keyless (`Authorization: Bearer public`; any other unauthenticated key 401s, measured 2026-08-22). ONE shape: the proxy path — Zen's own Anthropic surface (/v1/messages) serves free models TEXT-ONLY (any request carrying `tools` upstream-errors [1210] on every free id tested) while its OpenAI surface (/v1/chat/completions) carries function-calling, streaming and tool loops, verified end-to-end including a real `claude` child completing tool-bearing work. Proxy is LiteLLM (uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]' --with 'fastapi<0.120'; newer fastapi removed get_flat_dependant and this LiteLLM imports it), started PER DISPATCH from a generated config pinning exactly one deployment under the requested id — unknown ids fail routing loudly ('No deployments available'), there is NO alias surface, so unlike the codex transport the child's own modelUsage.canonicalModel IS trustworthy identity evidence. costModel is marginal-usd WITH $0-AUTHORED PRICES because the calls ARE $0 (`cost:"0"` in every Zen response); the legal costModel set has no 'free', and plan-quota would require a quota-capable capacityProbe nothing here can satisfy — so costUSD 0.0 in records is measured truth, not the pricing artifact it would be on a priced model. Privacy: Zen documents some free ids as permitted to train on submissions during their free period — check its Privacy section before dispatching proprietary material. ONE row on this transport (muse) is Contributor-Free rather than anonymous-free: it needs a real logged-in-account key (credentialVar below), trains on submissions by design, and 500s under the anonymous `public` bearer — see the muse model row's own comment.

anthropic._comment: The HOST transport, added 2026-09-04. These rows claim their tiers in `roles`, which the ladder's role cells must match (`--check`). No baseUrl: the child talks to Anthropic directly. No credentialFile: each plan's credential is its login's own OAuth on disk at `<configDir>/.credentials.json`, which an env scrub does not touch -- see anthropic_sidecar.sh, which deliberately inverts the scrub's original intent (gotcha_claude_code_entrypoint_leaks_host_auth_to_child) for this one route.

anthropic-console._comment: The primary Console organization's promotional credit, spent through an inference key rather than a login: NO `.credentials.json` exists for this plan, and `credentialVar` names the key the launcher exports to the child as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. `configDir` still names a directory of its own -- the child runs with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to it so no host login can win the auth race -- but nothing logs in there; `sync_plan_config.py` syncs its user config files and never touches credentials. No workspaceIdVar: an inference key needs no workspace header. `credit` is the owner-entered cycle (D4); the re-anchor state and the spending ledger live on the machine, not here. The probe (S3) prices this route's ledger rows against `credit`, and an unanchored, stale or unpriced cycle reads unreadable -- never as a zero-spend reading -- so the route is refused rather than guessed at.

Structural --check verifies the launcher, the key's presence and the plan's fields; --check --deep dispatches one turn and prices it into the default ledger.

driverNotes.text: Work unattended: never stop to ask. On a multi-item job, keep a per-item checklist and return only when every item has a disposition. A failed tool call is not a blocker: a truncated read, an edit whose anchor matches twice, a chained command that stops early, a path that is missing. Retry it another way (Read in parts, a longer anchor, each command on its own, a search for the path) and carry on. Report an item under couldNotSatisfy only when every route you can name has failed, and name the routes tried.

'gated' means 'the credential must not be the public placeholder' (enforced by opencode_sidecar.sh's explicit check), not a dollar floor: this transport declares `capacityUnsupported`, so the zero floor is allowed and launcher eligibility remains authoritative.

The launcher reads this field and builds litellm_params.model as 'openai/responses/<id>' instead of 'openai/<id>' -- the litellm prefix that forces the Responses call type end-to-end verified through a live proxy on the Anthropic Messages surface, not just the SDK. A small max_tokens (native Claude Code dispatches never send one) starves the reasoning-token budget on this call type and fails distinctly (`max_output_tokens` error, not a 500) -- unrelated to the apiMode fix itself.
